title: Easy Spiralizer Recipes for a Weight Watchers Diet
meta_description: Discover easy weight watchers spiralizer recipes that use a vegetable spiralizer for low‑carb meals. Quick, healthy dishes for your WW points.
html:
If you’re counting points on Weight Watchers, a vegetable spiralizer can be your secret weapon. Turning zucchini, carrots, and other veggies into noodle‑like strands adds volume without the carbs, keeping meals satisfying and within your daily allowance. Below are simple, tasty weight watchers spiralizer recipes that let you enjoy pasta‑style dishes while staying on track.

Why Spiralized Veggies Work for Weight Watchers

Spiralized vegetables are low in calories, high in fiber, and pack a lot of volume. That means you can eat a larger portion without blowing your points. The texture mimics traditional pasta, so you get the comfort of a familiar dish without the gluten or starch. Using a hand‑held or countertop Vegetable Spiralizer lets you prep these meals in minutes, perfect for busy weeks.

Spiralizer Basics: Choosing the Right Tool

Both handheld and countertop models work, but the choice depends on how often you’ll use it. Handheld units are portable and quick for one‑off tasks, while countertop spiralizers handle larger batches and give you more blade options (spaghetti, fettuccine, ribbon). Whichever you pick, make sure the blades are sharp and the assembly is easy to clean – a must for frequent use.

Recipe 1: Zucchini “Spaghetti” with Tomato Basil Marinara

This classic low‑carb favorite is simple, flavorful, and perfect for a Week 1 Weight Watchers plan.

  1. Spiralize 2 medium zucchinis using the spaghetti blade.
  2. Pat the noodles with a paper towel to remove excess moisture.
  3. In a skillet, sauté 1 minced garlic clove and ¼ cup diced onion in 1 tsp olive oil until translucent.
  4. Add 1 cup crushed tomatoes, a pinch of red pepper flakes, and fresh basil leaves. Simmer 5‑7 minutes.
  5. toss the zucchini noodles in the sauce for 2‑3 minutes until just warmed.
  6. Serve with a sprinkle of grated Parmesan if desired (optional for points).

One serving is about 2 WW points, depending on the amount of cheese used.

Recipe 2: Carrot “Fettuccine” with Lemon‑Garlic Shrimp

Bright, citrusy, and protein‑packed, this dish balances carbs, protein, and flavor.

  • Spiralize 3 large carrots using the fettuccine blade.
  • Season 8 oz peeled shrimp with salt, pepper, and a dash of paprika.
  • Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a pan, add shrimp, and cook 2‑3 minutes per side.
  • Remove shrimp, add 2 minced garlic cloves, ¼ cup chicken broth, and the juice of one lemon. Reduce for 1 minute.
  • Stir in the carrot noodles, toss for 2 minutes, then return shrimp to the pan.
  • Garnish with chopped parsley.

This portion comes in at roughly 4 WW points, thanks to the shrimp and a modest amount of oil.

Recipe 3: Mixed Veggie Noodle Stir‑Fry

Combine zucchini, carrot, and cucumber spirals for a crunchy, colorful stir‑fry that’s perfect for a quick lunch.

Ingredients:

  • 1 zucchini, 1 carrot, 1 cucumber – spiralized into thin ribbons.
  • ½ cup sliced bell pepper.
  • 2 tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce.
  • 1 tsp sesame oil.
  • 1 tsp grated ginger.
  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional).

Method:

  1. Heat the sesame oil in a wok over medium‑high heat.
  2. Add ginger and bell pepper; stir‑fry 1 minute.
  3. Add the spiralized veggies and soy sauce; toss for 3‑4 minutes until just tender.
  4. Remove from heat, sprinkle sesame seeds, and serve.

This dish is about 1‑2 points per serving, making it an excellent snack or side.

Tips for Keeping Spiralized Meals Light and Flavorful

  • Don’t overcook. Veggies lose their crunch and release water, which can make the dish soggy.
  • Use herbs and spices. Fresh basil, cilantro, or a dash of smoked paprika adds depth without extra points.
  • Add protein wisely. Grilled chicken, shrimp, or tofu keep you full and fit within the WW points system.
  • Mind the oil. A teaspoon of olive or sesame oil is usually enough for flavor.

FAQ

Can I freeze spiralized vegetables?

Yes, but it’s best to blanch them briefly (30 seconds) first, then freeze on a tray before transferring to a bag. Thaw and pat dry before reheating.

Do spiralized vegetables count as carbs on Weight Watchers?

They do contain carbs, but the fiber content is high, so they typically count as a low‑point food. Always refer to your WW app for exact values.

Is a handheld spiralizer as effective as a countertop model?

For single‑serving tasks or quick snacks, a handheld spiralizer works fine. For larger batches or multiple blade options, a countertop unit like the Vegetable Spiralizer offers more versatility and speed.
